biological.citation: Lymphocyte-Specific Function of the DNA Polymerase Epsilon Subunit Pole3 Revealed by Neomorphic Alleles (PMID: 32553171)
biological.summary: Pole3-null mice survive to late embryonic stages, so Pole3 is dispensable for DNA replication. Hypomorphic and neomorphic alleles show a stage-specific role for the Pole3 histone fold domain in T and B cell development. Adding positive charges to the acidic C terminus causes peripheral lymphopenia of increasing severity, pointing to non-replicative, cell-type-specific functions.

biological.citation: The genetic and biochemical basis of human leading strand synthesis (PMID: 41339636)
biological.summary: CRISPR screens in POLE4-null cells, together with biochemistry and structural modelling, identified a synthetic lethal interaction between POLE3-POLE4 and CHTF18-RFC2/5. POLE3-POLE4 "grips" newly synthesised dsDNA to support Polε processivity, in parallel with CHTF18-RFC2/5-dependent PCNA loading. Losing both is incompatible with leading strand synthesis and viability.

biological.citation: The Pole3 bidirectional unit is regulated by MYC and E2Fs (PMID: 16403426)
biological.summary: Pole3 expression in serum-stimulated NIH3T3 cells peaks at S-phase entry. Its bidirectional promoter, shared with C9orf46, has an E box and E2F sites. ChIP showed phase-specific binding of E2F1/4 and MYC to the promoter, so Pole3 is co-regulated with core histones during DNA synthesis.

biological.citation: Asymmetric distribution of parental H3K9me3 in S phase silences L1 elements (PMID: 37938774)
biological.summary: The HUSH complex interacts with Pol ε to promote asymmetric transfer of parental H3K9me3 to leading strands at head-on LINE-1 elements. Cells deficient in POLE3 or POLE4 lose H3K9me3 asymmetry and show increased LINE expression.

biological.citation: Requirement of WDR70 for POLE3-mediated DNA double-strand breaks repair (PMID: 37682991)
biological.summary: POLE3 interacts with CHRAC1 to promote DNA repair, by regulating homology-directed repair proteins and KU80 recruitment. A colorectal cancer CHRAC1 D121Y mutation weakens the POLE3 interaction and impairs repair. H2BK120ub1 and H3K79me2 at the POLE3 locus depend on WDR70 and on POLE3 transcription.

biological.citation: Stable inheritance of H3.3-containing nucleosomes during mitotic cell divisions (PMID: 35523900)
biological.summary: The Pole3-Pole4 pathway, alongside Mcm2-Pola1, takes part in transferring parental H3.1 and H3.3 histones after DNA replication. Pole3 and Pole4 mutants defective in parental histone transfer show chromosome segregation defects.

biological.citation: A consensus set of genetic vulnerabilities to ATR inhibition (PMID: 31506018)
biological.summary: Genome-scale CRISPR/Cas9 screens found that loss of the Polε accessory subunits POLE3 and POLE4 causes marked hypersensitivity to ATR inhibitors.

biological.citation: MMS22L-TONSL functions in sister chromatid cohesion in a pathway parallel to DSCC1-RFC (PMID: 36622344)
biological.summary: A genome-wide CRISPR screen in DSCC1-KO cells showed that they require POLE3 for survival. Co-depleting DSCC1 and POLE3 additively impairs DNA replication, so the two factors support leading-strand replication in parallel.

biological.citation: Orthoxenografts of Testicular Germ Cell Tumors Demonstrate Genomic Changes Associated with Cisplatin Resistance and Identify PDMP as a Resensitizing Agent (PMID: 29618620)
biological.summary: POLE3 and AKNA were the only two genes in the 9q32-q33.1 region deregulated in cisplatin-resistant testicular germ cell tumors carrying the 9q32-q33.1 gain. This links POLE3 expression to acquired cisplatin resistance.

biological.citation: USP15 Promotes Pancreatic Cancer Progression and Cisplatin Resistance By Activating DNA Damage Repair (PMID: 41950365)
biological.summary: USP15 binds POLE3 (confirmed by Co-IP) and suppresses its ubiquitination-dependent degradation. This stabilizes POLE3, promotes DNA damage repair and drives cisplatin resistance in pancreatic cancer cells.
